text: Saboyá is a town and municipality located in the Western Boyacá Province, within the Colombian department of Boyacá. The name Saboyá is of Italian origin and was introduced by European colonizers. Prior to the Spanish conquest of the Muisca in the central highlands of the Colombian Andes, the area was governed by a cacique named Saboyá. Pedro de Galeano, who was the brother of Martín Galeano and a soldier in the army of Hernán Pérez de Quesada—brother of the Spanish conquistador Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada—served as the first encomendero of Saboyá. Modern Saboyá was officially founded on October 4, 1556. Simón Bolívar visited the town on three separate occasions: January 2, 1821; September 6, 1827; and June 9, 1828. The primary economic activities in Saboyá are agriculture and livestock farming, with cultivated products including potatoes, maize, and fruits such as curuba, blackberries, tree tomatoes, and strawberries. The geographical coordinates of Saboyá are 5°42′N 73°46′W (5.700°N 73.767°W).
